q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS TOTAL_VIEWS FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1, 2 ) X WHERE TOTAL_VIEWS > 1 ORDER BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS TOTAL_VIEWS FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1, 2 ) X WHERE TOTAL_VIEWS > 1 ORDER BY 1
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID and also calculates the COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) as TOTAL_VIEWS. The HAVING clause in Q1 checks if the count of distinct ARTICLE_IDs is greater than 1, while in Q2, it checks if TOTAL_VIEWS (COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID)) is greater than 1. The difference lies in the grouping and the condition applied in the HAVING clause.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in the results between Q1 and Q2 can be observed when there are multiple VIEW_DATEs for the same VIEWER_ID, and the count of distinct ARTICLE_IDs is greater than 1. In this case, Q1 will return the VIEWER_ID for each VIEW_DATE, while Q2 will return the VIEWER_ID only once, as it groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID.
